title: Successful increment from an arbitrary configuration
statement: Let $k$ be a natural number, let $x,w,v$ be Boolean words, choose a work tape $i\in\mathrm{Fin}(k)$, and let $d$ be a configuration on input $x$. Suppose incrementing $w$ yields $v$, the state of $d$ is the run phase, and on tape $i$ the cells from the head position minus one through the head position plus $|w|$ agree with the buffer tape storing $w$ at the corresponding relative positions. After exactly $2m+2$ steps, where $m$ is the length of the initial run of true bits in $w$, the state is the done phase with true verdict, and the tape contents are those of $d$ except that the chosen tape stores $v$ in the interval of $|w|$ cells starting at its initial head position; no earlier time is in either done phase. At every time up to and including that bound, the chosen tape's head lies between one cell left of its initial position and $m$ cells right of it, inclusive, while every other tape head stays fixed.
hypotheses_covered: The state of $d$ is the run phase
For each integer offset $p$ with $-1\le p\le |w|$, tape $i$ at its head position plus $p$ agrees with the buffer tape storing $w$ at $p$
The exact run time is $2m+2$, where $m$ is the length of the initial run of true bits in $w$
No earlier time is in either done phase
For all tapes and times up to the bound, the selected head lies in the stated interval and the other heads remain fixed
